title: Topological dimension of a quasi-separated space is computed by an etale scheme atlas, including after base change
statement: Let $B$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $f:X\to B$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Assume $f$ is quasi-separated: its representable diagonal $X\to X\times_BX$ is quasi-compact, meaning that its pullback to any scheme is a quasi-compact scheme morphism (inverse images of quasi-compact open subsets are quasi-compact). For any morphism of schemes $T\to B$, put $X_T=X\times_BT$ [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Let $a:U\to X_T$ be a representable surjective etale morphism with $U$ a scheme [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Give $|X_T|$ its atlas topology [def-a1-space-point-topology], and use topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] for both $|X_T|$ and the underlying space $|U|$. Then $\dim|X_T|=\dim|U|$. Empty spaces have dimension $-\infty$. No finite-type, quasi-compactness, connectedness, or equidimensionality assumption is imposed on $X_T$ or $U$.

source.place: Tag 0A4J, lemma-dimension-decent-space (2); spaces-properties.tex Tag 0A4H, lemma-dimension-decent-invariant-under-etale (3), with Tags 04N5 and 04N6, definitions of chart dimension; quasi-separated morphisms remain so after base change by spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 03KL, lemma-base-change-separated. Over affine opens of the scheme T, the resulting space is quasi-separated; hence it is Zariski locally quasi-separated and is decent by Tag 03JX, lemma-bounded-fibres.

proof.text: Put $Y=X_T$ and $g:Y\to T$. The fibre-product node supplies $Y$ as an algebraic space. Via its structure map $g$ we regard $Y$ as an algebraic space over $T$: restriction to $T$-schemes is an equivalence between algebraic spaces over $B$ with a map to $T$ and algebraic spaces over $T$, which keeps the same etale scheme charts, hence the same point set, atlas topology and local rings. The diagonal $\Delta_g:Y\to Y\times_TY$ is the pullback of $\Delta_f:X\to X\times_BX$ along $Y\times_TY\to X\times_BX$: on every test scheme both sides classify the same pairs together with their equality in $X$. For a scheme $V\to Y\times_TY$, its pullback of $\Delta_g$ is therefore the pullback of $\Delta_f$ along the composite $V\to X\times_BX$, which is quasi-compact by the hypothesis. Thus $g$ is quasi-separated. Equivalently, any further scheme test preserves this property by quasi-compact base change. This uses no quasi-separatedness of $T$ as an absolute scheme.

source.place: Tag 03KL, lemma-base-change-separated: diagonal base-change identity; quasi-compactness on scheme tests by Tag 01K5, schemes-lemma-quasi-compact-preserved-base-change. Change of base scheme: spaces.tex Tag 04SG, lemma-category-of-spaces-over-smaller-base-scheme.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-space-topological-dimension-local-rings] with base scheme $S=T$ and space $Y$. Step 1 verifies exactly its relative diagonal hypothesis. It gives $\dim|Y|=\sup_{y\in|Y|}\delta_Y(y)$. Its definition of $\delta$ gives $\delta_Y(a(u))=\dim\mathcal O_{U,u}$ for every $u\in U$, since $a$ is an etale scheme-source map. Independently [lem-pc-scheme-dimension-local-rings] gives $\dim|U|=\sup_{u\in U}\dim\mathcal O_{U,u}$, without any quasi-separatedness requirement on $U$. By [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus], representable surjectivity of $a$ implies that $|a|:|U|\to|Y|$ is surjective.

source.place: Tag 0BAN, lemma-dimension, (1)=(2), and Tag 04NA, definition-dimension-local-ring; decent-spaces.tex Tag 0A4J, lemma-dimension-decent-space (2). Point surjectivity is spaces-properties.tex Tag 03H5, lemma-characterize-surjective.

proof.text: For every $u$, the value $\dim\mathcal O_{U,u}=\delta_Y(a(u))$ occurs among the terms of the supremum for $Y$. Conversely every $y$ has a preimage $u$, so its value $\delta_Y(y)$ occurs among the terms for $U$. The sets of values coincide, hence their suprema in $\{-\infty,0,1,\ldots,\infty\}$ coincide. The equalities from step 2 prove $\dim|X_T|=\dim|U|$. This argument also covers an unbounded set of finite values and the value $\infty$. If $Y$ is empty then the existence of $a$ forces $U$ empty, and if $U$ is empty its surjectivity forces $Y$ empty; both suprema are then empty and equal to $-\infty$.
